newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: UK, Philippine police team up against child sex.
newsitem.headline: UK, Philippine police team up against child sex.

text.p: A team of British detectives specialising in cases of child sex abuse said on Friday they had established information links with Philippine police to strengthen the fight against paedophiles.
"In terms of the Philippines, U.K. nationals are not among the top of the list," Detective Superintendent Bryan Drew of Britain's National Criminal Intelligence Service said.
"But we are of the view that even one paedophile from the U.K. is one too many," said Drew, who led the British team visiting the Philippines.
Since last year, when the Philippines toughened its drive against paedophiles, one Briton has been convicted and jailed on charges of sexually abusing children.
Drew said the British team had made contact with officers of the Philippine National Police and the country's premier law enforcing agency, the National Bureau of Investigation.
The contacts would help the two countries to exchange information on British paedophiles visiting the Philippines, he said.
Britain has recently introduced a bill in parliament to enable prosecution of Britons charged with committing child sex crimes abroad. The bill is awaiting approval.
The vulnerability of many children due to poverty in the country has made the Philippines a common destination for paedophiles, many of whom come on organised sex tours.
The Thai-based End Child Prostitution in Asian Tourism (ECPAT) estimates the Philippines has around 300,000 children working as prostitutes, although Filipino estimates are lower.
The visit to the Philippines by British intelligence officials follows a training course for Filipino policemen conducted by detectives of London's Scotland Yard last year.
